BiblicalUsage: hâçâh turns up where the Bible says to hush, to be silent, to still. In Numbers 13:30, the text says "And Caleb stilled the people before Moses." In Nehemiah 8:11, the text says "So the Levites stilled all the people."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hâçâh matters because God's Word means what it says, and this word is part of how He speaks plainly to us. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
